> **Notional system.** KESTREL is fictional. The names, dates, and decisions below are invented to show a System Security Plan as it stands before the system is built.

# KESTREL System Security Plan (SSP)

*Generated by `tools/ssp/build.py` from the System Description, the CCSD, the SADD, the Security Implementation Plan, the governing plans, the board's status snapshot, and the narratives in `tools/ssp/narrative/`. Edit those, not this page.*

This plan records what KESTREL actually does for each outcome its SADD selected, and what remains planned. It is organized by outcome, like the SADD and the Security Implementation Plan, so every outcome traces across all three by the same ID. The control-by-control view is the [SCTM](../05-sctm/index.md). The same content is kept as OSCAL in [`kestrel-ssp.oscal.json`](kestrel-ssp.oscal.json).

## 1. Purpose and Source

This SSP records how KESTREL has implemented the tailored control set that SADD version {{SADD}} designed, and that Security Implementation Plan version {{SIP}} selected products and sequencing for. KESTREL is not yet built, so every outcome is planned. Each narrative describes the planned implementation in the future tense, and each one closes with the Security Implementation Plan record that schedules it. As work reaches Done on the board, its outcome's status changes here, and its narrative is rewritten in the present tense to describe what was actually built.

An assessor can read this plan for orientation without the SADD or the Security Implementation Plan open beside it. Full traceability still runs back to both by outcome ID.

**Status today.** {{STATUS_SUMMARY}}

## 5. How to Read Each Outcome

Section 6 tells how security works in KESTREL, one focus area at a time, in the SADD's order. Each capability opens with a short overview, and each in-scope outcome follows as a few paragraphs of plain prose. The rigid detail lives elsewhere. The [SCTM](../05-sctm/index.md) is the control-by-control checklist, and the [Security Implementation Plan](../04-sip/index.md) names each product.

**Tense shows status.** A narrative for planned work says what KESTREL will do. Once the work is built, the narrative is rewritten to say what KESTREL does. An outcome with no narrative yet shows its schedule in italics.

**Each outcome closes with one small line.** It gives the outcome's status, its controls as a bare list, its Security Implementation Plan record, and the governing plan sections that hold its specifics.

- **Status** comes from the board. An outcome is Planned while none of its work is Done, Partially Does once some is, and Currently Does when its story is Done. Does Not applies only where a POA&M item records a deliberate gap.
- **Controls** are carried from the outcome's mapping in the SADD, which holds the reasoning for each.
- **Details** come from each governing plan's own trace lines, so they change only when a plan does.

## 7. Distribution and Protection

This plan names what KESTREL implements and what it does not yet, so it is a targeting aid to anyone who obtains it. It is CUI and is shared only with the AO, the SCA, the CSSP, the ISSM and ISSOs, the PMO ISSE, and the team leads. The CSSP and the SCA receive it under their agreements. No copy leaves the program's Confluence space or the configuration-controlled repository without the ISSM's approval.

**Approved By:** Pending. The ISSM submits the SSP to the AO with the authorization package. A draft accompanies the request for the interim authorization to test in Phase 1.

**Approval Date:** Pending.

---

## 9. Periodic Review and Revision

**Review Cadence:** Annually, as a floor, and with each continuous monitoring cycle's status report.

**Revision Triggers:**
- An outcome reaching Partially Does or Currently Does, which adds its narrative
- A significant change found under Security Impact Analysis (`GV-5.11`)
- A new version of the CCSD, the SADD, or the Security Implementation Plan
- A change to a governing plan section this plan points to
- An assessment finding that a narrative no longer matches what is built
- A product substitution recorded in the Security Implementation Plan

---

## 10. Machine-Readable Authoring

**Authoring format:** OSCAL generated from source.

The sources listed at the top of this page generate both this page and [`kestrel-ssp.oscal.json`](kestrel-ssp.oscal.json), an OSCAL 1.1.2 system security plan. Nothing is edited in either output, so the two cannot drift apart. The OSCAL file also carries the SCTM's control rows, so KESTREL keeps one machine-readable plan rather than two. Each build is validated against NIST's SSP schema with `tools/oscal/validate.py` before it is committed.
